topic: What happens if you try to build a nuclear shelter underground?
title: NUCLEAR
SHELTER?

script.text: لكن تحت الأرض، ليست كل الأخطار متساوية.
انفجار: ضغط، حرارة، غبار مشع. تحت الأرض يخفف، لا يلغي.
الثاني: الكتلة. تراب وخرسانة بينك والإشعاع.
الخلاصة: تحت الأرض يخفف، لا يضمن. ادخل، ابقَ، تابع.

science.claim: A nuclear detonation produces three distinct hazards: blast pressure/wind, thermal radiation, and radioactive fallout.
Fallout consists of radioactive particles (sand-like dust) sucked up by a ground burst; it arrives ~10-15 minutes after detonation and can extend 10-20 miles.
Underground/basement sheltering with mass between you and outside reduces fallout exposure significantly (protection factors up to ~200 for center of large buildings).
Radiation decays rapidly: over 80% of fallout energy released within the first 24 hours.
Ventilation matters: a sealed shelter risks hazardous air; mechanical ventilation at ~5 cfm/person is desirable; fuel-burning devices should be avoided.
Entranceways should force radiation to make at least two right-angle turns to scatter intensity.
No improvised shelter guarantees survival in a nuclear explosion.
